summary: D-1 is sound: callingRange is Array.filter over the input (or the input itself when the result is empty), so an equal length means the same elements in the same order. Same hero, board and opponents give the same canonical input and seed, so the result or RangeError kept from the whole-range run is exactly what the base's second run would have produced. Outcomes are keyed by attempt-array identity, and only attempts the whole-range run actually reached are kept. Non-RangeErrors are never kept. D-2 is gated by `defaultEquity && ranges.length >= 7`, inside the non-reused branch only. Injected seams always get the narrowed arrays and plain `run`, so their path is unchanged. The SPEC-05 test checks the threshold at 7 vs 6 opponents (8 and 7 seats), so an off-by-one would fail. SPEC-03 fails if reuse is removed (actions spot) or applied too broadly (HU unseen expects 2 runs). SPEC-04 fails if the seam is reused or rebudgeted. SPEC-02 deep-equals against the injected two-run path. Timing stays opt-in: perf file shows 4 skipped with no env, and the new files have no clock calls. Both new test files pass. The <7 delta bucket shows 0 differences at both sizes. No BLOCKER or MAJOR.
